PNN-003 Alibi on a short leash

Two walks. One tight alibi.

Two Tightie Whities. Two dogs. A few minutes apart. PNN examines a routine walk that became considerably less routine when somebody asked a follow-up question.

Subject team
Tightie Whities
Opened
October 7, 2026 at 9:46 PM (America/Denver)
PNN threat rating
Suspiciously well exercised

The incident

An anonymous source out walking their dog reported encountering two different members of the Tightie Whities, each also walking a dog, heading downhill just a few minutes apart. One team member's dog ownership came as news to the witness. Asked how long they had owned the dog, the member appeared, in the witness's estimation, to struggle for an answer. A simple walk had acquired a surprisingly difficult history section. PNN notes that 'How long have you had your dog?' is not usually considered an advanced question.

Suspected motive

PNN theory: leave a secret team meeting in staggered departures, or scout a future prank under cover of canine exercise. Separate the departures. Bring a dog. Look casual. A promising plan, defeated by the advanced investigative technique of saying hello twice. The alleged operation had accounted for timing, distance, and canine support. It had not budgeted for a neighbor with a memory.

Investigator's note

In Clueso's fictional reconstruction, a ribbon of toilet paper trails from one operative's shoe: the Tightie Whities attempting to leave no trace while providing their own paper trail. He has labeled it 'Operation Loose End.' The dogs, at least, remembered their roles. Clueso remains irritated that the Prowling Purrpetrators have supplied neither a confession nor anything this easy to follow.

Official PNN assessment

Clueso's assessment of the suspected operation: elaborate departure plan, insufficient rehearsal for casual conversation. The Tightie Whities appear to have prepared for everything except 'Nice dog. How long have you had it?' PNN recommends a full dress rehearsal of saying hello. Until then: two walks, one tight alibi, and a cover story still being house-trained.
